newsitem.title: USA: United adds second Chicago-London flight.
newsitem.headline: United adds second Chicago-London flight.

text.p: United Airlines said Tuesday it will add a second daily flight on a permanent, year-round basis between London's Heathrow Airport and Chicago's O'Hare International Airport, beginning September 1.
Previously, United had approval from the U.K's Department of Transport for the second flight on a seasonal basis for this summer only.
United is a unit of UAL Corp.

United said it will operate both daily flights with Boeing 777 aircraft, offering 292 seats in a three-class configuration. Currently, United offers service on the route with both Boeing 777 and 206-seat Boeing 767 aircraft.

"We are pleased to win indefinite approval for the second daily flight, which otherwise would have ended this October," Mark Schwab, United's general manager for the United Kingdom, said in a statement released from London.
He added that, as early as last year, United had been limited by the U.K. government to one daily flight to Chicago using its smallest trans-Atlantic aircraft.
